memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger." (Proverbs 15:1 )

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Anger never comes naturally or by its own accord. Usually, there must be a catalyst before you to kindle this within you. They can be a friend or a foe, your closest wife or husband, mother or father, teacher or student, manager or worker, doctor or patient this list goes on and on. But the main theme remains the one: this anger is sparked by any of these people before you. Knowingly or unknowingly, they will make you angry, and soon after, you will fall victim to that web filled with angry words, enter into arguments, and end up with fury, high blood pressure, and severe exhaustion. The person who caused it will soon go away, but you cannot; you will be trapped in mere tension and block out. Anger is a powerful acid that damages the very vessel in which it is stored.
Choosing patience over retaliation is highly beneficial, and it is certainly not a sign of weakness it is your self-preservation. Quit the place before the argument gets hotter. It will make your life smoother, protecting your peace of mind and health.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "Anger is an acid that can do more harm to the vessel in which it is stored than to anything on which it is poured." — Mark Twain

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, grant us the grace to recognize when irritation tries to take root in our hearts. When we are provoked, give us the wisdom to stay calm, the strength to choose patience, and the courage to walk away from needless strife. Protect our bodies and minds from the toxic nature of anger, and fill us with Your eternal peace. In Jesus' name, Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Do not let anyone else's negativity ruin your peace today. Protect your inner vessel, choose patience, and gracefully walk away from unnecessary conflicts.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: "The Dance of Anger" .
recommended_book.author: Harriet Lerner
recommended_book.quote: A practical guide that explains how to transform patterns of anger and respond rather than react.
